title: SLO-style thinking
text: Define expected availability and latency targets only after measuring real workloads. A target should be paired with a service-level indicator and an explicit interpretation of what counts as an error or unavailable response.

title: Failure correlation
text: When a latency spike occurs, correlate Prometheus data with NGINX access logs, FastAPI logs, Kubernetes events and PostgreSQL activity. A single metric rarely proves root cause.

title: Evaluation dashboard
text: The project requires a dashboard comparing system variants. It should show retrieval metrics, answer metrics, security results, latency and resource usage, with a clear corpus/benchmark/version selector so results are not mixed across incompatible runs.

title: Reference request path
text: A representative enterprise path is client -> NGINX/TLS -> FastAPI -> query processing -> hybrid retrieval -> reranker -> context selection -> generator -> citation verifier -> response. PostgreSQL can store structured metadata and experiment state, while a vector index stores dense retrieval data. Prometheus monitors the runtime. Docker packages services; Kubernetes and Helm can deploy them; GitHub Actions can build, test and promote artifacts.

title: Trust boundaries
text: Treat client queries, uploaded documents, retrieved passages and external model outputs as untrusted data. Deployment credentials, tool permissions, system instructions and monitoring administration belong to a higher-trust control plane. The RAG security layer must prevent retrieved instructions from crossing that boundary.

title: Version axes
text: Formal evaluation requires separate versions for corpus snapshot, benchmark, chunking/index configuration, retriever, reranker, generator, prompt/configuration and serving image. Changing any one of these can change results.

title: Resource boundaries
text: The serving system should isolate expensive generation and indexing operations from lightweight API and proxy processes. Resource requests and limits should be based on measurements. Formal latency results should record hardware and concurrency.

title: Deployment boundaries
text: A container image is an immutable application artifact; Helm/Kubernetes define deployment state; NGINX exposes the HTTP edge; FastAPI defines the service contract; PostgreSQL holds structured state; Prometheus observes behavior. Clear boundaries make experiments and failures attributable.

title: Corpus-to-answer trace
text: A robust answer trace should identify which corpus snapshot was indexed, which retriever and reranker selected passages, which citations supported claims and which model generated the answer. This is more useful than logging a prompt alone because it makes provenance auditable.

title: Hidden-benchmark protection
text: The mentor-controlled hidden benchmark should not be baked into training artifacts, public CI outputs or production dashboards. Evaluation infrastructure should make it technically difficult to accidentally mix hidden questions with the development corpus.

title: Change approval
text: Changes that can move the formal benchmark should be explicit: data changes, index changes, model changes and prompt/configuration changes. Record the hypothesis, change and evidence so the final report can explain why each improvement was kept.

title: Failure containment
text: A parser failure should not take down the API; a broken exporter should not stop request handling; a model timeout should not exhaust every API worker; a failed database connection should produce a bounded error instead of an infinite retry loop. This is the operational meaning of component isolation.

title: One command evaluation
text: The final project should have one documented command that identifies the versions, runs the frozen benchmark, measures retrieval and answer metrics, stores results as JSON/CSV and produces charts. CI and dashboards should consume these machine-readable results rather than reimplementing the experiment logic.

title: 502 from NGINX to FastAPI
text: Check NGINX upstream address and port, then test the upstream from the NGINX runtime. Confirm FastAPI is listening on the container interface, inspect the API process exit state and review container logs. Only after connectivity is confirmed should you investigate request-time behavior.

title: FastAPI times out during generation
text: Measure whether time is spent before retrieval, in retrieval, in reranking, in model generation or while waiting for a database call. Check concurrency and resource pressure. Apply bounded timeouts and consider background workers or queueing for workloads that are not request/response sized.

title: Kubernetes Service has no endpoints
text: Check the Service selector against Pod labels, then inspect Pod readiness. A healthy-looking Pod can still be excluded from a Service if labels do not match or readiness is false.

title: Helm upgrade produces unhealthy Pods
text: Inspect the rendered manifest, release history, changed values, Pod events and logs. Compare the new image/configuration with the last successful revision. Do not assume Helm itself is the root cause.

title: PostgreSQL query becomes slow
text: Capture the actual SQL and parameters, run `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` safely, inspect row estimates, indexes, locks and I/O. Check whether a recent schema or data distribution change invalidated an earlier assumption.

title: Prometheus dashboard goes blank
text: Check whether the target is still being scraped, whether the metric name or labels changed, and whether the query expects a series that no longer exists. Distinguish a zero value from missing data.

title: Docker container keeps restarting
text: Inspect the exit code and logs, then check environment variables, mounted files, permissions and dependency availability. If the process exits cleanly, inspect the command/entrypoint and container orchestration restart policy.

title: Linux host is out of disk
text: Use `df` to identify the full filesystem, `du` to find large paths, and inspect container images, writable layers, logs, model files and database storage. Free space only after determining what the deleted or growing data represents.

title: TLS works locally but fails through NGINX
text: Compare certificate hostname, certificate chain, protocol versions and NGINX certificate/key configuration. Test from an actual client path rather than only from localhost. Confirm the private key is readable by NGINX and that configuration reload succeeded.

title: RAG answer cites irrelevant documents
text: Check the retrieval top-k, hybrid merge behavior, reranker ordering and chunk metadata. Evaluate whether the error is retrieval recall, reranker precision, query formulation or an out-of-date/contradictory source. The correction should be linked to the component that actually caused the miss.
